english.notes:
From 20th October 2014, the power to issue a closure notice under section 1 of the Anti-social Behaviour Act 2003 is no longer in force. The repeal does not, however, apply in relation to a notice issued before that date or anything done in connection with such a notice. As such, this offence can still be committed in relation to a notice issued before 20th October 2014.

A person does not commit this offence if he has a reasonable excuse for entering or being on the premises (as the case may be). (Section 4(4)).

other.powersofarrest: A constable in uniform may arrest a person he reasonably suspects of committing or having committed this offence (section 4(5)).
other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
